title: Introduction to information security in government
summary: Connect information protection to reliable, fair public services and to the DISO's actual mandate.
outcomes: Explain confidentiality, integrity and availability through a service.
Map information and ownership across organisational boundaries.
Prepare an actionable DISO decision brief.

realExample.title: SARS's completed 2025 auto-assessments
realExample.documentedOutcome: SARS reported on 18 July 2025 that it had completed 5.8 million auto-assessments, compared with five million in 2024.
realExample.discussion: Examine how source accuracy, appropriate disclosure and access to a correction channel affect the public value of automated decisions.
realExample.scope: A documented processing outcome. The classroom analysis does not assert undisclosed SARS controls or that every assessment is error-free.

units.title: Information protection begins with the service
objectives: Identify the information supporting a public decision.

chapters.title: Begin with the resident's purpose
chapters.bodyHtml:
A resident needs a housing-benefit decision before a rent deadline. The service includes an application, supporting documents, eligibility rules, staff decisions, payment instructions and a way to challenge mistakes. A server inventory misses much of this work. Begin with the public outcome, the decisions needed to achieve it and the information each decision uses.

Include paper forms, telephone records, email, spreadsheets and contractor-held copies. A confidential record that is inaccurate can deny a person a benefit. An accurate record that cannot be reached by the deadline can also cause harm. Information security protects the trustworthy handling and usefulness of the information across this complete service.

Give each important information asset a named business owner, purpose, affected people, location, authorised users and service dependency. The owner should understand its meaning and permitted use. The person maintaining a database is not automatically the person authorised to decide how its records may be used.

chapters.title: Make the three objectives concrete
chapters.bodyHtml:
Confidentiality concerns authorised disclosure. Integrity concerns accuracy, completeness and authorised change. Availability concerns timely, dependable access by authorised users. In the benefit service, emailing bank details to unnecessary recipients affects confidentiality; changing an account without authority affects integrity; an outage at the payment deadline affects availability.

An incident can affect all three. Stolen administrator credentials might expose documents, alter payments and disable the service. Conversely, blocking every user to prevent disclosure imposes an availability cost. Effective protection must allow the legitimate service to operate.

Translate objectives into decisions: who may view bank details, who approves a change, how approval is checked and how long the service may be unavailable. Then choose evidence that demonstrates those conditions. This makes control selection assessable rather than a discussion of product labels.

chapters.title: Follow the information through dependencies
chapters.bodyHtml:
Map transfers, copies and changes of responsibility. Identity services, connectivity, supplier support, payment interfaces and records staff may each become the point of failure. Include notice to the resident and correction of disputed information, not only initial processing.

The SARS case provides a real example of information-dependent service at scale. Ask how an incorrect source record or unavailable correction route would affect a citizen. These are analytical questions; a reported processing count does not establish the effectiveness of every security control.

Rank dependencies by consequence and time. A delayed newsletter and an interrupted emergency payment may use the same platform but need different responses. State who is affected, what harm develops, how quickly it develops and which alternative channel is usable. These observations become inputs to risk assessment.

application.title: Map the fictional Khanyisa relief-payment service
application.instructionsHtml:
District offices scan paper forms; a central team checks eligibility; a supplier hosts the case system; Finance sends a weekly payment file. Residents appeal by telephone. Last month's payment file remains on a district shared drive.

Spend about 60 minutes drawing the flow and identifying six assets, their owners and one confidentiality, integrity and availability consequence.
application.deliverable: A service map and six-row asset/consequence table.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Include applications, documents, rules, decisions, payment instructions and appeal records. Show the supplier and shared-drive copy.

Unnecessary shared-drive access exposes bank details; an unapproved payment edit may divert relief; inaccessible appeal records prevent timely correction. Allocate business use to the relief-service owner and payment approval to Finance, with ICT supporting the controls.

A valid answer traces the complete service, including copies and corrections. A list of devices alone is insufficient.

reflection.prompt: Which information asset in your service is overlooked because it lives outside the main application?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Describe a fictionalised example, its owner and the consequence of failure.

quiz.title: Information protection begins with the service — knowledge check

questions.name: M01-U01-Q01
questions.promptHtml: An accurate grants database is unavailable throughout the payment deadline. Which objective is directly affected?

answers.textHtml: Availability
answers.feedbackHtml: Availability includes access when the service needs it.

answers.textHtml: Confidentiality
answers.feedbackHtml: No disclosure is described.

answers.textHtml: Integrity
answers.feedbackHtml: The records remain accurate.

answers.textHtml: Classification
answers.feedbackHtml: A label does not explain timely access.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Availability includes access when the service needs it.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q02
questions.promptHtml: What is the most useful starting question for a new service?

answers.textHtml: What public outcome depends on which information?
answers.feedbackHtml: Understand the service before selecting controls.

answers.textHtml: Which security product does the incumbent supplier recommend?
answers.feedbackHtml: A product recommendation follows an understanding of the service and information need.

answers.textHtml: Which controls can be copied unchanged from the last project?
answers.feedbackHtml: The new service's purpose and dependencies must be understood before reusing controls.

answers.textHtml: Which department owns the largest part of the infrastructure budget?
answers.feedbackHtml: Budget responsibility does not define the public outcome or information requirements.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Understand the service before selecting controls.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q03
questions.promptHtml: An unauthorised edit replaces a beneficiary's bank account. What is the primary failure?

answers.textHtml: Integrity
answers.feedbackHtml: Integrity includes authorised change.

answers.textHtml: Confidentiality, because bank details are personal information
answers.feedbackHtml: The scenario's direct failure is an unauthorised change; disclosure would be a separate confidentiality issue.

answers.textHtml: Availability, because a payment may later be delayed
answers.feedbackHtml: Delay can be a consequence, but the initial control failure is the integrity of the bank record.

answers.textHtml: Authentication, because every incorrect record proves the user was unidentified
answers.feedbackHtml: An identified or compromised account can still make an unauthorised change.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Integrity includes authorised change.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q04
questions.promptHtml: Who should own the meaning and business use of eligibility information?

answers.textHtml: The responsible service manager
answers.feedbackHtml: Ownership follows the service and its decision authority.

answers.textHtml: The database administrator solely because they maintain the tables
answers.feedbackHtml: Technical maintenance does not itself confer authority over the information's business meaning.

answers.textHtml: The DISO solely because the information is sensitive
answers.feedbackHtml: The DISO advises on protection; the responsible service owner understands and authorises business use.

answers.textHtml: The hosting supplier under an ordinary infrastructure contract
answers.feedbackHtml: Hosting responsibility does not automatically transfer information-use authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Ownership follows the service and its decision authority.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q05
questions.promptHtml: The service map omits a contractor's monthly export. What should be added?

answers.textHtml: The copy, purpose, recipient and retention dependency
answers.feedbackHtml: Follow information across its actual boundaries.

answers.textHtml: Only the contractor's company name, without the copy's purpose or lifecycle
answers.feedbackHtml: The service map also needs the information flow and handling responsibilities.

answers.textHtml: Only exports that are stored inside departmental premises
answers.feedbackHtml: Contractor-held information remains part of the service's information handling.

answers.textHtml: A note that the database remains authoritative, with no further treatment of the copy
answers.feedbackHtml: An authoritative database does not remove the risks and obligations associated with another copy.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Follow information across its actual boundaries.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q06
questions.promptHtml: What does the SARS case's assessment count establish?

answers.textHtml: A documented scale of delivered processing
answers.feedbackHtml: Keep a case claim within its source's scope.

answers.textHtml: That the processing volume proves every underlying control was independently audited
answers.feedbackHtml: The source reports a delivered processing count, not that assurance conclusion.

answers.textHtml: That the same architecture will meet every other department's service requirements
answers.feedbackHtml: A scale example does not establish suitability for a different service.

answers.textHtml: That every automatically processed case required no later review or correction
answers.feedbackHtml: The count does not establish the final correctness of every individual case.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Keep a case claim within its source's scope.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which entries strengthen an asset register? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A named business owner
answers.feedbackHtml: This gives decisions an accountable home.

answers.textHtml: The consequence of unavailability
answers.feedbackHtml: This connects the asset to the service.

answers.textHtml: A product inventory with no information purpose or owner
answers.feedbackHtml: Technical inventory alone does not establish business responsibility or impact.

answers.textHtml: A uniform criticality label assigned without assessing service consequences
answers.feedbackHtml: Meaningful prioritisation requires the actual impact of the asset's loss or misuse.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Ownership and consequences support prioritisation.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which observations show that protection extends beyond computers? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: A paper file can disclose personal information
answers.feedbackHtml: Protection is not medium-specific.

answers.textHtml: A telephone appeal record can affect a person's rights
answers.feedbackHtml: Decisions rely on varied records.

answers.textHtml: A claim that approved encryption removes the need to track paper copies
answers.feedbackHtml: Encryption of one channel does not protect every form of the information.

answers.textHtml: An assumption that supplier-held exports fall outside the department's information map
answers.feedbackHtml: Information handling continues across organisational and technical boundaries.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Follow information across media and organisations.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q09
questions.promptHtml: One event can affect confidentiality, integrity and availability.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: A compromised account may expose, alter and interrupt information.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. A compromised account may expose, alter and interrupt information.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: A compromised account may expose, alter and interrupt information.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Blocking all legitimate access is a successful outcome whenever it prevents disclosure.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Availability and lawful service delivery remain important.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: Availability and lawful service delivery remain important.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Availability and lawful service delivery remain important.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the observation to its concept.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: The first three are objectives; ownership identifies a decision role.

questions.name: M01-U01-Q12
questions.promptHtml: Begin with the public [[1]], then map its [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Service purpose and information needs guide the work.

units.title: The DISO's mandate and working relationships

chapters.title: Influence across distinct authorities
chapters.bodyHtml:
The 2022 information-security Directive provides for the Head of Department to delegate an official to perform the DISO function, accountable to the GITO for departmental information security. Start with the written delegation and actual departmental structure.

The DISO works with service owners, ICT, risk, legal and privacy specialists, records staff, HR, procurement and communications. These roles intersect but are not interchangeable. DISO appointment does not automatically make someone the statutory Information Officer or the approver of all expenditure.

For a payment-system weakness, the service owner explains consequences; ICT proposes controls; the relevant authority decides resources and residual risk. The DISO connects the evidence to these decisions and follows the response into operation.

chapters.title: Advice that leads to a decision
chapters.bodyHtml:
A useful brief identifies the service, observed condition, evidence, consequences, options, recommendation and decision owner. Separate facts from assumptions. If an account appears shared, describe the observed account use and what needs confirmation rather than asserting that every transaction was fraudulent.

Address legitimate urgency. For temporary district access, propose named users, limited permissions, expiry and review instead of forcing a choice between account sharing and service failure. Make the remaining risk and permanent correction visible to the authorised owner.

Record an action owner, due date, expected evidence and escalation trigger. A meeting agreement starts the action; a functioning control or a properly authorised revised decision supports closure. A closed ticket is meaningful only when its evidence matches the agreed outcome.

chapters.title: A first-month engagement rhythm
chapters.bodyHtml:
First, read the mandate and meet priority service owners. Ask what must continue under pressure, which records must remain trustworthy and where workarounds recur. Review existing risk registers, audit actions, incident summaries and continuity plans so known work survives the handover.

Next, follow two important information flows with operational staff. Compare written procedures with actual practice. A spreadsheet used to rescue a broken workflow may reveal an unmet service need and an unmanaged copy. Understand both before recommending a change.

Finish the month with a prioritised programme, accountable owners, decision dates and a reporting rhythm aligned to departmental planning. Include immediate protections and material improvements. Keep the work connected to service results rather than creating a separate document-production exercise.

application.title: Write a first-month DISO brief
application.instructionsHtml:
Eight clerks in a fictional department share a supplier support account because named-account approval takes three weeks. It can view every application and edit payment details. A payment deadline is two days away.

Spend about 60 minutes proposing a temporary measure and permanent correction, identifying who may decide each element.
application.deliverable: A one-page brief with an action and escalation table.
application.suggestedAnswerHtml:
Seek named limited access with expiry and independent payment-change approval while provisioning is repaired. Confirm technical feasibility before promising delivery.

The authorised owner decides temporary residual risk. The DISO advises and tracks; ICT and the supplier implement agreed controls.

Closure evidence includes actual permissions, shared-credential retirement and a usable permanent provisioning process. Escalate inability to protect payment changes.

reflection.prompt: Which decision is routinely assigned to the DISO even though another role owns it?
reflection.guidanceHtml: Explain how helpful advice can accompany a clear transfer to the authorised decision maker.

quiz.title: The DISO's mandate and working relationships — knowledge check

questions.name: M01-U02-Q01
questions.promptHtml: To whom is the delegated DISO accountable under the 2022 Directive?

answers.textHtml: The GITO
answers.feedbackHtml: Read the DISO–GITO relationship with the department's delegation.

answers.textHtml: The Information Officer, solely because both roles concern information
answers.feedbackHtml: The Directive names the GITO as the DISO's accountability route; the statutory Information Officer remains a distinct role.

answers.textHtml: The Chief Financial Officer, because security has a budget
answers.feedbackHtml: Budget responsibilities do not replace the Directive's stated reporting relationship.

answers.textHtml: The departmental risk committee as an unnamed collective owner
answers.feedbackHtml: A governance forum does not replace the named GITO accountability route.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Read the DISO–GITO relationship with the department's delegation.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q02
questions.promptHtml: What is missing from 'improve security urgently'?

answers.textHtml: A decision, owner and observable outcome
answers.feedbackHtml: Advice needs an accountable, assessable next action.

answers.textHtml: A more frequent status meeting without a defined result
answers.feedbackHtml: Meeting frequency does not supply the missing decision or outcome.

answers.textHtml: A detailed product specification before the service problem is agreed
answers.feedbackHtml: Technical detail cannot substitute for a clear purpose and accountable decision.

answers.textHtml: A risk score with no action owner or acceptance condition
answers.feedbackHtml: A rating alone does not make the instruction actionable.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Advice needs an accountable, assessable next action.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q03
questions.promptHtml: How should a suspected shared account be reported?

answers.textHtml: Describe the evidence and the uncertainty to resolve
answers.feedbackHtml: Separate facts and assumptions while retaining urgency.

answers.textHtml: Report the suspicion as a confirmed fraud finding before investigating intent
answers.feedbackHtml: An access observation does not establish fraud or intent.

answers.textHtml: Delay every response until the entire history of use is certain
answers.feedbackHtml: Known exposure can be addressed while uncertainty is investigated.

answers.textHtml: Close the concern on an administrator's verbal reassurance without examining the access
answers.feedbackHtml: Relevant operating evidence is needed to resolve the concern.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Separate facts and assumptions while retaining urgency.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q04
questions.promptHtml: Who may accept material residual business risk?

answers.textHtml: The authority designated by governance arrangements
answers.feedbackHtml: Acceptance follows a defined delegation.

answers.textHtml: The technical administrator because they can implement the setting
answers.feedbackHtml: Technical capability does not establish business risk-acceptance authority.

answers.textHtml: The DISO in every case solely by virtue of appointment
answers.feedbackHtml: Risk acceptance depends on the department's actual delegation and governance arrangements.

answers.textHtml: The supplier's project manager because the supplier operates the platform
answers.feedbackHtml: A supplier's operating role does not confer the department's business authority.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Acceptance follows a defined delegation.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q05
questions.promptHtml: Which is convincing access-control closure evidence?

answers.textHtml: The agreed named permissions and expiry operate
answers.feedbackHtml: Assess the actual agreed condition.

answers.textHtml: A meeting discussed access
answers.feedbackHtml: Discussion starts work.

answers.textHtml: A policy was emailed
answers.feedbackHtml: Distribution does not prove operation.

answers.textHtml: A ticket was relabelled closed
answers.feedbackHtml: The label needs evidence.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Assess the actual agreed condition.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q06
questions.promptHtml: Drag each role onto the responsibility it carries. A is information purpose and service outcome; B receives the DISO's accountability under the Directive; C advises on security risk and controls; D carries the relevant statutory information-officer responsibilities.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Keep the business purpose, GITO accountability, DISO advice and statutory Information Officer responsibilities distinct. Local delegations should map these roles explicitly.

background.alt: Drag each role onto the responsibility it carries. A is information purpose and service outcome; B receives the DISO's accountability under the Directive; C advises on security risk and controls; D carries the relevant statutory information-officer responsibilities.

drops.label: A: Owns the information purpose and the service outcome.
B: Receives the delegated DISO's accountability under the Directive.
C: Advises on security risk and control effectiveness.
D: Carries the relevant statutory information-officer responsibilities.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q07
questions.promptHtml: Which features belong in temporary access? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: Named user, narrow permission and expiry
answers.feedbackHtml: These make access controllable.

answers.textHtml: A permanent correction owner and due date
answers.feedbackHtml: The workaround connects to its underlying fix.

answers.textHtml: A shared account that expires but cannot identify its individual users
answers.feedbackHtml: Expiry alone does not preserve individual accountability.

answers.textHtml: An approval with no defined service scope because the access is temporary
answers.feedbackHtml: Temporary access still needs an explicit purpose and permission boundary.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Temporary arrangements need scope and a route to sustainable operation.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q08
questions.promptHtml: Which statements respect distinct roles? Select all correct answers.

answers.textHtml: The DISO supplies incident facts to legal and privacy owners
answers.feedbackHtml: Facts support their decisions.

answers.textHtml: The DISO confirms delegation before approving risk
answers.feedbackHtml: Authority must be known.

answers.textHtml: DISO appointment automatically confers statutory Information Officer status
answers.feedbackHtml: These are distinct roles.

answers.textHtml: All procurement authority transfers to the DISO
answers.feedbackHtml: Procurement follows its own delegation.

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Collaborate without conflating authorities.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q09
questions.promptHtml: A workaround can reveal both a service requirement and a security risk.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: Understand its purpose and protect the information as the process improves.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. Understand its purpose and protect the information as the process improves.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Understand its purpose and protect the information as the process improves.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q10
questions.promptHtml: Security planning should operate entirely separately from departmental planning.
questions.trueFeedbackHtml: This is incorrect. An isolated programme can lose business ownership and resources.
questions.falseFeedbackHtml: An isolated programme can lose business ownership and resources.
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: An isolated programme can lose business ownership and resources.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q11
questions.promptHtml: Match the contribution to its usual role.

pairs.promptHtml: Accept risk within a formal mandate

questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Collaboration preserves rather than erases the different responsibilities.

questions.name: M01-U02-Q12
questions.promptHtml: A useful action identifies its [[1]], due date and expected [[2]].
questions.generalFeedbackHtml: Owner and evidence connect a decision to its outcome.
